transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-20 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Dr. Ellen Park (Sunvale CTO), Marcus Lee (VP Eng), Aisha Brown (Security Lead), Ravi Patel (Platform Eng)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro, I'm Jordan, AE for Redwood, Priya's our solutions engineer. We'll spend most of the call on rate limits, quotas and how org/project keys work in the console and API.
[00:18] Ellen: Hi, thanks. We're really interested in strong per-team quotas, and also per-project billing so our product teams can't blow through the monthly spend.
[00:27] Marcus: We'll probably need a mixture of hard quotas and soft alerts. Also curious about burst allowances for spikes.
[00:34] Priya: Great. I'll share my screen in a sec and walk through the Console. But first, quick qualification: what's your expected steady RPS and peak burst?
[00:45] Ravi: For a pilot, steady is ~10 RPS per project, peaks to 200 RPS across all projects during batch jobs. Monthly tokens estimated 30M.
[00:56] Priya: Okay that's helpful. We recommend org-level quotas to cap overall spend, and project-level keys to isolate teams. That gives you per-project billing plus global backstops.
[01:10] Aisha: From security, we need audit logs, KMS integration, and SSO. Also want to ensure rate-limit evasion is auditable.
[01:20] Jordan: Yes — we have audit logs, can integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping, and SSO via SAML/SCIM for RBAC. We'll include notes in the security pack.
[01:28] Priya: Sharing screen now — console > org settings > rate limits. (screen noises) Sorry if the screen feed is a bit laggy.
[01:40] [01:40] Priya: At the top you see org quota block: "Monthly token cap", "Burst credit pool", and per-project quotas underneath. You can set hard caps (blocks traffic) or soft quotas (alerts + throttling).
[02:00] Marcus: How exactly is burst credit applied? If a project uses bursts, does it draw from org pool or isolated per-project bank?
[02:08] Priya: Good question. Default configuration draws bursts from a project-level bank up to its configured limit; if enabled, the org pool can act as an overflow. So you can prevent projects from borrowing org credits by toggling overflow.
[02:24] Ellen: Is that enforced at the gateway or at Redwood runtime? We don't want to rely on app-level controls.
[02:31] Priya: Enforcement is at the Redwood edge and runtime; it's independent of client-side behavior. Rate limiter is token-bucket based with per-key state and a centralized metrics stream to console. Occasionally the transcript will show 'token-bucket' transcribed as 'token basket' in our exports, sorry.
[02:47] Aisha: If you have a distributed runtime, how do you keep per-key counters consistent?
[02:53] Priya: We use a sharded counter approach with fast approximate reconcilers for strict windows. For high-frequency small windows we use local counters with periodic sync to reduce latency. There is some small leeway, usually within a few hundred milliseconds; if you need absolute precision we can run in a stricter mode (higher coordination cost).
[03:14] Ravi: That leeway — could it impact billing accuracy?
[03:18] Jordan: Billing alignment is separate; tokens for billing are recorded centrally and are the source of truth. The enforcement leeway is for rate decisions; billing uses aggregated usage to the minute so we've not seen drift affecting invoicing.
[03:32] [03:32] Priya: Now demo: create a new project key -> name it 'clinical-notes-sandbox' -> set project quota 5M tokens/month -> set QPS limit 20 -> enable burst allowance 50 with overflow disabled.
[03:50] [04:00] Marcus: How do you handle accidental key leaks — can we rotate keys automatically?
[04:06] Priya: Yes, key rotation is supported via the console and API. You can create short-lived keys for dev environments. Also we've got project-level RBAC so only certain roles can create or rotate keys.
[04:18] Ellen: Can we enforce per-model quotas? For example, GPTx-large uses more tokens and we want different caps.
[04:26] Priya: You can set usage-based quotas by model tag. There's a "policy" layer where you create rules: project X can't call model family A more than Y tokens/day. You can also tag models as premium and bill separately.
[04:38] Marcus: What's the behavior if a project hits quota mid-request? Do you allow the request to finish?
[04:44] Priya: You can choose between three policies: fail-fast (reject new requests once quota exceeded), drain-through (allow in-flight requests to complete but reject new ones), or soft-throttle (slow down responses). Default for hard caps is fail-fast, but you can set drain-through for customer-facing flows.
[04:59] Aisha: For compliance, we need proof of enforcement — logs that show the exact decision.
[05:05] Priya: All enforcement decisions are logged with key, project, rule id, and timestamp; logs are available in the console and exportable to your SIEM.
[05:14] [05:14] Jordan: Quick note on dedicated capacity — if you move to Redwood Dedicated, you get isolated GPU pools and dedicated rate-limit instances. That reduces noisy neighbor effects for consistent latency.
[05:28] Ravi: If we start hosted and then move to Dedicated, any migration effort on keys or quotas?
[05:33] Priya: The abstraction is the same. Keys and policies move with your org config; we'll help export/import policy configs. There may be some capacity planning for throughput, but minimal changes to keying or client calls.
[05:46] Marcus: Any limits on number of projects or keys? We expect dozens of teams.
[05:51] Priya: Hundreds of projects are supported. We recommended grouping ephemeral dev work under a single dev project to keep management simpler.
[06:00] Ellen: How do we get per-project invoices? We want to chargeback to product teams.
[06:05] Jordan: We provide per-project usage breakdown in the billing dashboard and can generate CSVs with line-item tokens and cost. For enterprise contracts we can set billing granularity per-project and integrate with your billing system.
[06:17] Marcus: Regarding enforcement algorithms, you mentioned token bucket. Do you support fixed-window as well?
[06:22] Priya: Yes, token bucket is our default for smooth throttling, but we offer fixed-window for simpler rate capping needs. Fixed-window is slightly more bursty at window edges, so depends on your requirement.
[06:36] [06:36] Ellen: Any integration to alerting? We use PagerDuty and Datadog.
[06:40] Priya: Exports to Datadog, Datadog metrics and webhooks, also PagerDuty for quota-exceeded alerts. You can configure alerting thresholds per project or org.
[06:50] Aisha: Encryption and audit — do you store keys locally?
[06:54] Jordan: Keys are encrypted at rest using CMKs and we support customer-managed KMS. Audit logs are write-once and can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[07:05] Marcus: Demo request — show how to change a project's quota and observe enforcement in real-time.
[07:10] Priya: Sure. I'm opening the project's detail page -> increasing monthly cap from 5M to 10M -> I apply the change. Console shows policy applied. Now we can run a small poke traffic to show enforcement toggles.
[07:24] [07:24] (sound of test traffic)
[07:28] Priya: On the right, realtime metrics show requests accepted vs throttled. You can also view the decision log for each request.
[07:36] Ravi: Nice. If we wanted to programmatically update quotas, is there an API?
[07:40] Priya: Yes, all console actions are backed by REST APIs. We'll share the endpoint docs.
[07:46] Jordan: Quick interjection — some customers do dynamic quotas using our API to expand quotas during a deploy window, then shrink back after. Works well for predictable bursts.
[07:59] Marcus: About the cost: if a project exceeds its quota and borrows from org overflow, how is that billed?
[08:06] Jordan: Borrowed tokens are billed to the project; the org overflow is just an enforcement mechanism. The billing CSV will show which tokens were billed under borrowed/overflow categories.
[08:18] Aisha: What about rate-limit bypass for internal system calls? We have internal orchestration that must always succeed.
[08:24] Priya: You can create service keys with higher priority and whitelist IPs or CIDR blocks; service keys can be exempt from some quotas but are audited.
[08:34] Marcus: Any caveats with SDKs? Do client SDKs handle 429s gracefully?
[08:39] Priya: SDKs implement exponential backoff and retry helpers. For streaming we provide clear error codes when throttled so the client can present UI feedback.
[08:50] [08:50] Ellen: Security follow-up: can we disable project creation by product teams unless approved?
[08:56] Jordan: Yes, you can enforce an approval workflow via RBAC; only admins can create projects by default.
[09:04] Priya: Also, templates: you can lock quota templates so teams start with predefined caps.
[09:10] Marcus: Let's talk about SLOs — our p95 latency target is 250ms for completions under 512 tokens. Can Redwood guarantee that under host mode?
[09:20] Priya: For hosted, we publish performance profiles per model. If you need strict p95 guarantees, Dedicated capacity is better; we offer SLO-backed tiers. We'll include published profiling during follow-up.
[09:33] Jordan: One more item — Redwood Optimize can suggest quota configurations based on your traffic patterns to reduce cost and avoid wasted headroom. It can recommend project caps and burst settings.
[09:44] Marcus: That sounds useful to avoid manual tuning.
[09:47] [09:47] Aisha: Any security docs you can share?
[09:50] Jordan: Yes, I'll attach our SOC2, ISO, and KMS integration docs in the follow-up email.
[09:57] Ellen: Ok next steps — we'll share traffic profile and acceptance criteria.
[10:02] Jordan: Great. Recap: Jordan sends pricing + security pack, Priya shares console video and API snippets, Sunvale to share traffic and p95 targets, and we'll schedule a 1-hour benchmark next week.
[10:14] Marcus: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:18] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up by EOD Monday.
[10:22] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains minor auto-transcription errors (names, product bits). Console demo included a live metrics panel and policy changes. Customer is evaluating both hosted and Dedicated for later stage if SLOs demand it.
